## 1. Narrative Arc

The story FDJ United tells about itself changed character completely over these three calls, and the change is the whole point.

In **March 2025**, the tone was triumphal and offensive. Management had just rebranded the old French lottery monopoly (Française des Jeux) into "FDJ United," a self-styled "European champion in the gaming industry," on the back of the debt-funded takeover of Kindred (the Unibet/32Red online betting group). By **July 2025**, the language pivoted hard from offense to defense. Revenue on a like-for-like basis (as if Kindred had always been owned) was already *down 2%*, and the new vocabulary was "transition year," "cost efficiency plan," "performance plan," and "regulatory headwinds" in the UK and Netherlands. Management introduced the "Play Forward 2028" plan with a softened medium-term goal of ~5% organic revenue growth by 2028 (i.e. not now).

By **February 2026**, the defensive crouch was complete. Pallez openly conceded 2025 was "significantly impacted by major adverse factors" — tax increases in France, the Netherlands and Romania worth "more than €50 million" — and described Dutch regulation as "ill considered." The growth-driver language of March 2025 (omni-channel accounts, new retail banners, EuroMillions momentum) is still present but now functions as reassurance, not as a thesis. 🔴 Net debt ~€1.47B where the balance sheet was net cash before Kindred; first-ever bond issuance.

🟢 Sales-force internalization and tech-stack (KSP) migration are structural margin levers that genuinely complete by 2027.

- The rebrand from "Française des Jeux" (a French national institution) to "FDJ United" (a pan-European betting group) is itself a tell: management chose to dilute the safest, highest-margin asset they own — a state lottery monopoly — by stapling it to a lower-margin, heavily-regulated, tax-exposed online betting business. The diversification narrative masks a *mix shift toward worse economics*.
- The word "happily" slipped out (Feb-26) when the CFO noted UK revenue is 85% online casino — said just before the new UK casino tax bites hardest there. A small, revealing stumble.
- Repeated deferral language ("2027," "2028," "by the end of 2027") across all three calls signals the team itself does not expect the numbers to look good in the near term.
- Management's near-relief that they are "not at all in the sports betting U.S. market" — framed as prudence — also quietly admits FDJ United has no exposure to the one large growth market its online peers are chasing.

**Trajectory: DETERIORATING (with a durable core).** This is a high-quality lottery monopoly being slowly diluted and out-run by a permanent, escalating tax/regulatory assault on the gaming sector it chose to expand into. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **the headline cheapness (≈7.4x price-to-free-cash-flow) is priced against a base of earnings that is structurally shrinking on the taxed parts, not a temporary dip — so the discount must be earned segment by segment, not taken at face value.**

**Economic moat: NARROW, and the trend is ERODING.** The moat *type* is a regulatory license — the French lottery concession is a true legal monopoly (genuinely wide and durable on that segment alone). But the consolidated entity's returns are unmistakably falling (EPS −56% YoY, gross margin contracting, ROIC high but declining), because management bolted a thin-moat, tax-exposed online betting business onto the monopoly. On the blended evidence the durable earnings base is narrow and being compressed.

**Secular threat: MATERIAL (not yet terminal).** The structural force is *regulatory-rent / reimbursement-style compression* — governments across France, the UK, the Netherlands and Romania are legislating the tax take on gross gaming revenue sharply higher (French online casino 21%→40% in a single step), permanently lowering the cash each euro of stakes returns to operators. This is the gaming-sector analogue of healthcare reimbursement cuts: a policy-driven, cohort-wide de-rating, not a tech disruption and not a cyclical dip. The lottery monopoly insulates terminal value from being *destroyed*, which is why this is material rather than terminal — but the cheapness is substantially a sector-wide fear-print shared with every regulated gaming peer, not idiosyncratic single-name alpha.

Revenue on a like-for-like basis (as if Kindred had always been owned) was already *down 2%*, and the new vocabulary was "transition year," "cost efficiency plan," "performance plan," and "regulatory headwinds" in the UK and Netherlands. Management introduced the "Play Forward 2028" plan with a softened medium-term goal of ~5% organic revenue growth by 2028 (i.e. not now).

By **February 2026**, the defensive crouch was complete. interrogator_dossier:
# FDJ United (FDJU.PA) — Forensic Dossier

*Prepared for the investment committee. Live price used: €21.93 (Euronext Paris, EUR), near the 52-week low of €20.61 vs a high of €29.02. Market value about €4.05B; enterprise value about €5.5B after roughly €1.47B of net debt (borrowings plus leases, cash netted).*

FDJ United is the rebranded Française des Jeux: a French lottery and retail sports-betting monopoly (the LSF unit, run under an exclusive 25-year state concession) bolted to a competitive pan-European online betting-and-gaming arm (the OBG unit) assembled through the 2024 acquisition of Kindred (Unibet, 32Red). Roughly three-quarters of revenue and nearly all of the profit come from the protected French lottery; the online arm is the growth-and-risk bet.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the three calls (2024 annual results on 2025-03-06, H1-2025 on 2025-07-30, and 2025 annual results on 2026-02-19) the story moved from *"transformational acquisition"* to *"absorbing the blows."* In March 2025 the tone was celebratory — a new group identity, the Kindred deal closed, the European Commission's state-aid investigation resolved with "no state aid" and only a €97M adjustment, and a 15% dividend increase. By July 2025 the frame had shifted to defending a tough comparison base (Kindred's Euro-2024 quarter) and reassuring on full-year guidance. By February 2026 management was openly cataloguing "major adverse factors": gambling-tax increases in France, the Netherlands and Romania (over €50M of combined revenue-and-profit hit), plus an "ill-considered" Dutch regulatory tightening that shrank the legal Dutch market about 25%. The growth narrative was quietly replaced by a cost-and-margin narrative: a self-help efficiency plan that management raised twice — from an initial €20M for 2025, to about €50M actually delivered, then a multi-year target lifted from €120M to €150M of recurring savings by 2028.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Profitable and sustainable growth"; revenue multiplied 1.8x since 2019 | Revenue did grow (2021 €2.26B → 2025 €3.68B, +20% in 2025 on Kindred consolidation) | Matches on the top line — but the growth is bought, not organic |
| Strong, resilient earnings | Net income fell from €425M (2023) and €399M (2024) to €176M (2025); reported EPS €2.23 → €0.95, down 56%; 5-yr EPS CAGR −11.4% | Diverges sharply — reported earnings are in retreat |
| "Solid financial results… good return to shareholders" | Dividend still raised to €2.10 (about 80% of *adjusted* net income); adjusted net income (~€486M implied by the payout) held roughly flat, so the reported collapse is heavily purchase-price amortization and one-offs | Half-true: cash-to-shareholders is real, but rests on an adjusted figure that strips large non-cash and "one-off" items |
| Record cash generation | Management cited "record operating cash flow generation of nearly €300M" for 2025; the screener's trailing free cash flow reads €923M | Do not trust the €923M in isolation — it is far above management's own ~€300M and likely inflated by player-balance/working-capital timing; normalized free cash flow is more plausibly €400–550M |
| Efficiency plan on track | Delivered ~€50M in 2025 vs €20M promised; target raised to €150M by 2028 | Green flag on execution so far — but the payoff is back-end-loaded to 2027–28 |

The central forensic tension: this is optically very cheap (about 7.6x price-to-free-cash-flow, roughly 6x enterprise value to EBITDA) yet the reported profit line is falling fast, and the gap between the two is fiscal — the French and European states are progressively taxing away the monopoly rent.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining / turning defensive.** March 2025: offensive and expansionary ("we want to be a European champion"). July 2025: managing expectations, leaning on "sequential improvement" and one-off exclusions (a €14M employee-share-plan charge, a €20M one-off tax). February 2026: candid damage-control — "our results were significantly impacted by major adverse factors… this is not a surprise." Management stays specific and does not hide the headwinds, but the language has clearly migrated from growth and investment to cost, efficiency and margin defense.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium-to-High.** Management has hit its markers: 2025 full-year guidance (stable revenue vs 2024 pro-forma, EBITDA margin above 24%, net-debt reduction over €150M) was delivered — 24.5% margin, net debt down. The efficiency plan over-delivered (~€50M vs €20M). The screener shows an 80% earnings-beat rate (4 of 5 quarters). The caution: the medium-term ambitions (about 5% organic growth by 2028, EBITDA margin above 26%) are a promise made while the near-term tape deteriorates, and 2026 guidance itself steps the margin *down* to 23–24%. They deliver on what they can control (costs); they cannot control the tax and jackpot cycle.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Analysts pressed repeatedly on (a) the size and jurisdiction of the tax drag — quantified at ~€90M for 2026 (UK ~€30M, rising above €40M in 2027; Romania ~€8M; French annualization) — which management answered squarely; (b) when the cost savings actually land, where management conceded the impact is "more in 2026… and more heavily in 2027"; and (c) the online-casino consultation in France, which management flagged as unlikely to reopen given the political environment. The recurring worry analysts circle is the one management cannot dispel: whether the French state will keep raising gambling taxes, converting a monopoly into a taxed utility.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 Reported EPS down 56% in 2025; net margin collapsed to 4.8%.
🔴 Serial gambling-tax escalation across France, Netherlands, Romania and now the UK — a structural, recurring headwind, not a one-time event.
🔴 2026 guidance steps margin *down* to 23–24%; the deterioration has not bottomed.
🔴 Piotroski 4/9 and Altman-Z 2.4 (grey zone) reflect the earnings and leverage strain from the debt-funded Kindred deal.
🟢 The French lottery is a genuine regulatory monopoly with a long exclusive concession, low-single-digit GGR growth and ~36% unit EBITDA margin.
🟢 State-aid overhang closed favorably (no state aid; €97M booked).
🟢 Investment-grade balance sheet (Moody's Baa1), leverage under 2x, deleveraging; dividend raised to €2.10 (~9%+ yield).
🟢 Cost plan over-delivering and raised to €150M.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The vocabulary shift from "growth" to "mutualization," "optimization" and "sales-force internalization" signals a company now competing on cost, not expansion. Management's comfort that it is *not* in the US sports-betting market ("we are happy not to be… already quite questioned about potential disruption") is a tell that the online-betting economics worry them. The repeated framing of tax and regulation as external and "ill-considered" is accurate but also positions any future miss as someone else's fault. Notably, capital allocation is turning inward — deleveraging and buying its own efficiency rather than further M&A ("not a significant priority for OBG").

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: DETERIORATING** (business direction), executed by a **credible, candid** management team. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: this is not a broken franchise, it is a *taxed* one — the crown-jewel lottery keeps growing gross gaming revenue, but the state is capturing the incremental rent through repeated tax hikes, so cheap cash-flow multiples can persist for years because the after-tax base keeps getting skimmed. The re-rating, if it comes, is back-end-loaded to the 2027–28 margin-recovery story and requires taxes to stop escalating.

**Moat:** a regulatory-license monopoly in the lottery (wide and durable in isolation) blended with a competitive, no-moat online arm — net **NARROW** at the group level. **Moat trend: ERODING** — ROIC ~16.7% and net margin 4.8% are high-but-falling (net margin was ~13% two years ago; EPS down 56%), the classic signature of a compressing moat. **Secular threat: manageable** — the pressure is fiscal and regulatory (recurring gambling-tax extraction, Dutch-style market shrinkage, online competition), which compresses margins but does not extinguish the franchise; gambling demand endures and the lottery concession is intact. This is a fear-and-fiscal print with genuine cheapness, but the cheapness sits on a base the state is actively skimming — value with a real value-trap tail, not a clean mispricing.
